title: Lord! Thou Art Good: All Nature Shows
description: Lord! Thou Art Good: All Nature Shows in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Simon Browne wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 130 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Universal Goodness of God”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Lord! thou art good: all na-ture shows Its might-y Au-thor kind: Thy boun-ty through cre-a-tion flows, Full, free, and un-con-fined.

lines: Lord! thou art good: all nature shows
Its mighty Author kind:
Thy bounty through creation flows,
Full, free, and unconfined.
The whole, and every part, proclaims
Thine infinite good-will;
It shines in stars, and flows in streams,
And blooms on every hill.
We view it o'er the spreading main,
And heavens which spread more wide;
It drops in gentle showers of rain,
And rolls in every tide.
Through the vast whole it pours supplies,
Spreads joy through every part:
O, may such love attract my eyes,
And captivate my heart!
My highest admiration raise,
My best affections move!
Employ my tongue in songs of praise,
And fill my heart with love!

licence: Public domain: Simon Browne died in 1732.
credits: Words by Simon Browne (1680–1732), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
